method: Own actual source before lexical locators, then photographed full relevant1865Latin and actual1907grammar. Headform index used only to find photographs; no TEI/OCR meanings or modern/canonical English used.

items.own_assessment: Imperative to plural righteous addressees. Latin exspectare/sperare with shortened imperative and explicit96:1 supports hope/wait with hope, not a noun or third-person assertion. SourceAfI andWaweII remain as pictured; no extra internal syllable supplied.
Plural righteous used as address. Printed star editorial; not a lexical prefix.
Causal for/because attaches the ensuing destruction statement to the hopeful exhortation.
Adverb quickly/promptly. No date or bounded interval supplied.

Third-person plural nonpast reflexive/passive formation, agreeing with the following plural sinners. Perish/be destroyed available; not selected active they destroy. No destroyer supplied. Preserve sourceHaut rather than normalizing to lexiconHoi.
Plural sinners is the post-verbal subject, distinct from the vocative righteous/you.
From + before/presence with second-person plural suffix. Source does not itself name an additional agent. From before you/from your presence is a bounded English relation.
And + singular authority/power nominal subject. NahuVI source ending, not roughNahuI. SautVI pronged shape, notSatVI arch. No source subordinate noun for kings/judges supplied.
Third-person singular nonpast be/become, matching the singular abstract authority noun. Not a plural command or causative grant with a newly named giver.

To/for you with second-person plural suffix; with be and authority, a dative possession/availability relation. English authority will be yours or you will have authority can express this without adding a grantor.
Upon/over them with third-person plural suffix. Sinners are the preceding third-person plural subject; righteous are second-person addressees. Do not replace body them with apparatus you.
As/according to comparative-measure relation. Not an unmarked independent that-clause or permission to alter the final noun.
Will/desire noun with your second-person plural suffix. According to your will/as you desire available; not an independent perfect verb or a count of acts.

whole_meaning: Hopeful exhortation to the righteous because the sinners will quickly perish/be destroyed from before them; authority over the sinners will be to the righteous according to their will. The shift between plural addressees, plural sinners and singular authority is retained.
own_English_control_not_author_candidate: Hope, righteous ones, for sinners will quickly perish from before you; and authority over them will be yours according to your will.
scope_limits: This is own preparation, not a verdict on unseen author bytes. No approval of96:2–8 or whole chapter.
